description:
The oil seller’s hometown reaches the opening through a pie recipe and remembered food, not a world-map exposition scene. Its architecture, residents and wider role remain undeveloped; it is not established as either Koga settlement.

Proposed future recognition: the child notices blue reeds painted unevenly on bowls in ordinary kitchens, not an emblem reserved for a sacred order. A baker folds pastry scraps into a smaller pie rather than throwing them away. The seller’s recipe can be recognized by its folded edge before somebody tells the player where they are. A local may disagree about how much butter belongs in it; home memories need not be geographically exact. These details give the place a familiar taste and craft without fixing its location, population or wider quest.

data.description: The seller’s hometown is the existing source of the meal; extending the blue-reed household pottery motif here is a bible proposal, not magical heraldry.

sections: Sections 5–6: places and characters; working names versus identities
